doc.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: Joining Harry James in 1939 and what the job paid
summary: He sat in at the rehearsal and was hired; pay was eighty-five dollars, the same as with Norvo.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So you went with Harry James then.

From Red Norvo, yeah. Well, like Jerry Jerome said, “Harry James is having a rehearsal, so go up there,” which I did. And he says, “You got your trumpet with you?” I says, “Yeah.” I always went in town with the horn you know. And he says, “All right, after we take a break” he says, “you want to play, you want to sit in?” I says, “Yeah.” So I did. And after that he called me aside and he said, “Are you interested in joining the band?” and so forth. And I said, “Yeah, I’d love to.” So that was 1939, the year.
Can I ask you what he was paying?
No, you could ask me. Because before that I was getting eighty-five dollars a week with Red Norvo.
That’s not too bad for the time.

1938. It was great. So I went with Harry for the same money, like I don’t know. I guess eighty-five was the standard thing then. If you got a hundred that means you were a little special you know. Yeah. First trumpet player got a hundred. Second trumpet player got eighty-five.
